payload.title: tasks_root() resolver: one canonical write path for events.jsonl, the CAS lock and every rebuild_*.py (fixes 4 divergent copies + 1 orphaned event)
payload.description: Right now tasks/ has FOUR divergent copies of events.jsonl (main checkout + 3 worktrees) and the task.created for dotfiles-tsk-dispatch-launcher was orphaned in a worktree, never merged into the real log until manually recovered on 2026-09-21 (its event was silently dropped by a git merge conflict resolved 'prefer PR branch' on tasks/events.jsonl during PR #30's merge, commit 61473f7 -- an append-only JSONL log cannot be safely conflict-resolved by a plain textual merge). Root cause of the divergent-copies class of bug: append_event.EVENTS_FILE/LOCK_FILE and each rebuild_*.py's TASKS_DIR all derive from Path(__file__).parent, so a script copy running inside a worktree writes that worktree's log instead of the canonical one. Add lifecycle.tasks_root(): $TSK_ROOT if set (explicit opt-in -- this is how demo/run_demo.sh isolates the demo log and how tasks/ itself can be developed in a worktree against a scratch log), otherwise always ~/dotfiles/tasks regardless of where the .py file lives. Redirect ALL real write-path constants through it: append_event.EVENTS_FILE, append_event.LOCK_FILE, and TASKS_DIR in rebuild_kanban.py, rebuild_metrics.py, rebuild_graph.py, rebuild_view.py, rebuild_cards.py. Assert at import that LOCK_FILE and EVENTS_FILE share a parent -- if the events file is redirected and the lock file is not, two processes share the log while flocking different files and Layer-A CAS silently stops being atomic while still appearing to work. lifecycle.TASKS_DIR stays as is (it only feeds sys.path.insert, not a write path). No path-pattern guard: print one stderr line when tasks_root() is not the canonical path; if worktree detection is ever wanted, compare git rev-parse --git-dir with --git-common-dir, never a '.claude/worktrees/' substring (that only catches EnterWorktree-created worktrees, not manual git worktree add). payload.title: L2: claim protocol in a separate claims.jsonl -- locked conditional appends, closed role vocabulary, atomic preemption, human preempts swarm
payload.description: Give tasks/ real claims so concurrent sessions, teams and a future tsk daemon never silently work the same task. (1) Claims live in their own log tasks/claims.jsonl with its own sidecar lock tasks/.claims.lock, both gitignored (precedent: tasks/.events.lock). This is load-bearing, not cosmetic: append_event.last_event_id_for_task() does NOT filter by event type, so a claim written into events.jsonl would make the validation/done CAS abort with exit 3 and a misleading 'someone else moved this task first'; and lifecycle.project() setdefaults on any event carrying task_id, so a typo'd claim would materialise a phantom card. A separate log removes both by construction, and leaves the proven CAS untouched. Claims are live, machine-local, TTL-bounded state that is deliberately NOT durable -- losing claims.jsonl just means everyone re-claims; the audit trail stays in events.jsonl via --team/--handoff. No tsk daemon is required anywhere on the critical path. (2) Three record types: claim.acquired {claim_id, task_id, role, ttl_seconds, expires_at}, claim.released {claim_id, reason}, claim.preempted {claim_id, preempts, role, ttl_seconds, expires_at, reason} -- preemption is ONE append, so a task is never ownerless mid-transfer. actor/session_id/ts reuse the common envelope. TTL 4h for human/agent, 30min for swarm. (3) EVERY claim write takes flock(LOCK_EX) on .claims.lock and re-evaluates active_claims INSIDE the lock before deciding -- a check-then-write without the lock lets two sessions both see 'no claim' and both write, leaving two rival claims active forever, which is the exact failure this card exists to prevent. Inside the lock also: reject a task_id with no real task.created in events.jsonl (exit 2), and dedup on (task_id, actor.id, role) so a retry or crash-recovery RENEWS the existing claim_id (expires_at = max(current, requested); a renewal never shortens) instead of creating a rival claim the owner would then negotiate with itself. claim.released is authorised only for the claim's own actor.id, any human actor, or an already-expired claim. (4) lifecycle.py gains CLAIM_ROLES = ('implementer','reviewer','validator','planner') -- a closed vocabulary, because free-form roles filled by independent LLMs ('implementer' vs 'impl' vs 'dev') never collide and the default path becomes never negotiating -- plus SWARM_ACTOR_KINDS = ('swarm',), closing the gap where move_task.py's CLI already accepts swarm and lifecycle.py does not. PIPELINE_PHASES, LEGAL_TRANSITIONS, project() and last_event_id_for_task() are unchanged. Accepted, named risk: swarm has zero occurrences in the real log, so it is being canonised without any field use. (5) Escalation: no active claim -> claim; different role -> coexist; same role, different actor -> an interactive session asks the owning session synchronously over the cross-session channel, and only after a 2-minute silence blocks on a human with exactly three options: (a) let session B proceed anyway, in another worktree; (b) session B waits until A releases or confirms; (c) session B picks another backlog task. A NON-interactive actor never blocks on a human: expired claim -> take over with claim.preempted reason 'expired'; live claim -> skip the task, take the next backlog item, emit one best-effort async notification via the human-in-the-loop notification path, max 3 attempts per task per day. That sub-case is the only sanctioned use of the 4h-SLA async channel for claims; it remains the wrong tool for live conflicts everywhere else. (6) A swarm claim is always preemptible by a human (or an agent acting for one), never the reverse, via a single claim.preempted. The preempted actor re-checks its claim before every externally visible action (file write, git command, event append) and at least every 60s during long operations; on losing it, it aborts the current step, does NOT commit or push work in flight, leaves the per-task worktree intact for inspection, and exits. (7) Worktree rule: one worktree per claimed task for CODE; tasks/ is always written to the canonical root (guaranteed by dotfiles-tsk-tasks-root-resolver, not by discipline). On record: the 2026-09-21 wave1-parallel-dispatch session violated tasks/README.md:203-208 by writing tasks/handoff.md and running move_task.py from inside a worktree shared by five subagents -- the 4 divergent events.jsonl copies and the orphaned dispatch-launcher event (recovered 2026-09-21, see dotfiles-tsk-tasks-root-resolver) are the direct result. Full design: tasks/plans/claim-protocol.md (sections A-F), produced via a plan-orchestra run (5 parallel researchers, 1 adversarial critique round that found 12 material flaws in the first draft, all addressed in this v2).

payload.title: Custom git merge driver (merge=union or equivalent) for tasks/*.jsonl so a conflict resolution can never silently drop an append-only line
payload.description: Root cause found 2026-09-21 while investigating an orphaned event (dotfiles-tsk-dispatch-launcher's task.created, from PR #35): commit 61473f7, 'Merge origin/claude/session-handoff into tmp/pr-30-merge (auto-resolved: prefer PR branch)', resolved a real conflict on tasks/events.jsonl by taking the PR branch's version wholesale. That branch had been forked before PR #35 merged, so its tail of events.jsonl was shorter -- the merge silently discarded a real, already-merged event instead of reconciling both append tails. events.jsonl (and the planned tasks/claims.jsonl from dotfiles-tsk-claim-protocol) are append-only logs: a standard textual 3-way merge, and especially an 'ours/theirs' conflict resolution, is unsafe for this format because there is no correct way to line-merge two divergent tails without a semantic union. Fix: add a .gitattributes entry (tasks/events.jsonl merge=jsonl-union, tasks/claims.jsonl merge=jsonl-union once it exists) plus a custom merge driver registered in .git/config or via a versioned .gitattributes + driver script that unions both sides' lines (dedup by event_id/claim_id, sort by ts) instead of picking one side. Document the driver setup step in setup.sh so a fresh clone gets it automatically -- a merge driver in .gitattributes without the corresponding driver command registered locally silently falls back to git's default (textual) merge, which is exactly the failure mode this card exists to close. Verify with a deliberate two-branch-diverging-appends test before considering this done.

payload.title: Archive done tasks out of live views + reorganize tasks/ directory tree so 'current' stays small (no infinite memory/context)
payload.description: tasks/ grows unbounded by design (events.jsonl is append-only, kanban.md's Done section and tasks/cards/ only ever add entries) -- every session that reads tasks/README.md/CHEATSHEET.md/kanban.md for context pays that cost forever, and it compounds: this single session alone added 8 real cards (5 Wave 1 + 3 claim-protocol) plus 4 evaluation READMEs plus 2 plan docs (human-in-the-loop-notifications.md, claim-protocol.md) plus roadmap.md/.mmd plus per-task cards/. There is no infinite memory/context budget, so 'current' views need to stay small and only the true history needs to keep everything. Two parts: (1) ARCHIVAL: events.jsonl itself stays append-only and complete (it is the source of truth, never truncated) -- but the DERIVED, read-heavy views must stop showing everything forever. rebuild_kanban.py's Done column should only list tasks done within a rolling window (e.g. last 30 days) plus a count/link for the rest; older done tasks move to a generated (never hand-edited) tasks/archive/done-<year>-<month>.md, one file per month, so a session only ever loads 'what changed recently' by default. tasks/cards/ similarly needs a done/ vs active/ split (or a done card gets a frontmatter archived_at field the default listing filters out) so a fresh session's card sweep doesn't have to read every card ever created. metrics.md and roadmap.md need the same rolling-window treatment for the same reason. (2) DIRECTORY TREE CLEANUP: tasks/ has grown organically and inconsistently across this session's work -- tasks/evaluations/<name>/README.md (ad hoc, spike-specific), tasks/plans/<name>.md (design docs, mixed with the evaluations in spirit but a different directory), tasks/cards/<id>.md (generated, one per task, flat, will scale to hundreds), tasks/demo/ (a self-contained example, correctly isolated). Needs one documented, deliberate tree (a README.md in tasks/ that names every subdirectory's purpose and generation rule: which are source-of-truth/hand-written vs generated/never-hand-edited, which are pruned/archived and how, which are permanent). Update tasks/README.md and tasks/CHEATSHEET.md to match once the tree is decided. payload.title: Fix infinite recursion in ~/.local/bin/gh wrapper (duplicate PATH entry)
payload.description: ~/.local/bin/gh is a thin wrapper: mise use -g --quiet gh && exec mise x gh -- gh "$@". ~/.local/bin appears twice in PATH, both before mise's real gh install dir (~/.local/share/mise/installs/gh/latest/.../bin) -- so mise x gh -- gh resolves gh back to the wrapper itself, infinite self-recursion (confirmed via mise x gh -- which gh returning the wrapper path; high CPU, no network I/O, hangs indefinitely). Found and worked around 2026-09-21 by invoking the real gh binary by absolute path; the underlying PATH duplication + wrapper self-reference is still unfixed. Fix options: dedupe PATH in shell rc, or have the wrapper resolve the real binary path explicitly instead of relying on mise x's PATH injection.

Nunca instala/corre/da source a conteudo da comunidade -- e sempre dados, nunca instrucoes.

Pecas ja decididas (plan mode, revisto por um agente Opus adversarial antes de aprovar):
- omarchy-radar: comunidade Omarchy Linux Quattro (releases via feed do plugin mtolhuys/omarchy-news-radar + fallback GitHub API, commits/discussions do omacom/omarchy, awesome-omarchy, marketplace, reddit/HN).
